transcript: Hello, and thank you for being here today. My name is Alex, and I'll be guiding a short check-in conversation with you. There are no right or wrong answers, so just choose whatever feels closest to true for you. To start, how have you been feeling over the past couple of weeks?

option_text: Pretty good, overall
transcript: I'm glad to hear that. Even when things are going fairly well, it can help to check in with ourselves.

option_text: Okay, but up and down
transcript: That makes sense. A lot of people notice their mood shifting from day to day, and it's worth paying attention to.

option_text: Not great, honestly
transcript: Thank you for being honest with me. It takes courage to say that things haven't been easy.

option_text: I've been really struggling
transcript: I'm really sorry things have been so hard. I appreciate you trusting me with that, and we'll take this one step at a time.
I'd like to understand a little more about what's been on your mind. When you think about what has been weighing on you most lately, which of these feels closest?

option_text: School or work pressures
transcript: School and work can ask a lot of us. Deadlines, expectations, and the feeling that there's never quite enough time can really add up.

option_text: My relationships with other people
transcript: Our relationships matter so much to how we feel. When something is off with the people around us, it can affect everything else.

option_text: Bigger questions about life, or a general sense of stress
transcript: Those bigger questions, and that kind of stress without one clear cause, can feel heavy, even when they're hard to put into words.
When that stress shows up, people handle it in very different ways, and all of them are human. Which of these sounds most like what you tend to do?

option_text: Distract myself or try not to think about it
transcript: That's a very common way to cope. Stepping away can give us a break, although sometimes the stress is still waiting for us when we come back.

option_text: Make a plan and tackle the problem directly
transcript: It sounds like you like to take action. That kind of problem-solving can be a real strength.

option_text: Talk it through with someone I trust
transcript: Reaching out to others is a meaningful way to cope. Talking things through can make a problem feel lighter.
Let's talk about the people in your life. When things get difficult, how supported do you feel by the people around you?

option_text: I have people I can count on
transcript: It's really good to hear that you have people in your corner. That kind of support can make a big difference.

option_text: I have some support, but I don't always reach out
transcript: That's very understandable. Even when support is there, it isn't always easy to ask for it.

option_text: I mostly feel like I'm on my own
transcript: Thank you for sharing that. Feeling like you're on your own can be really hard, and I'd like to understand a little more.
When you feel on your own with things, what do you think makes it hardest to connect with other people?

option_text: I don't want to be a burden
transcript: Many people worry about that. Wanting to protect others is a caring instinct, and you deserve support too.

option_text: I'm not sure who I could talk to
transcript: That's an honest answer. Sometimes the first step is simply knowing what options are out there.

option_text: I prefer to keep things to myself
transcript: That's okay. Privacy matters, and it's important that any support you choose feels comfortable to you.
If you were to keep meeting with a therapist, what would you most want to get out of those conversations?

option_text: Learn practical skills and strategies
transcript: So it sounds like you'd like some practical tools, ways to manage stress and handle difficult moments when they come up.

option_text: Have a space to talk and be heard
transcript: So what matters most to you is having a space to talk openly and feel heard, without having to fix everything right away.

option_text: A bit of both, or I'm not sure yet
transcript: That's completely fine. Many people want some of both, and it's okay to figure that out along the way.

We're nearly at the end of our conversation. Today we talked about how you've been feeling, what has been on your mind, how you tend to cope, the support around you, and what you'd want from future conversations. Does that feel like a fair summary of what we talked about?

option_text: Yes, that feels right
transcript: I'm glad. Thank you again for talking with me today. In a moment, you'll be asked a few questions about our conversation. Take good care of yourself.

option_text: Partly
transcript: Thank you for telling me. There's always more to someone's story than a short conversation can capture. In a moment, you'll be asked a few questions about our conversation. Take good care of yourself.

option_text: Not really
transcript: I appreciate your honesty. A short conversation can't capture everything, and that's okay. In a moment, you'll be asked a few questions about our conversation. Take good care of yourself.
